ObjectName.value: Juan Pablo II, constructor de Paz

Categories.value: Popes|Self-published work|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Karol Wojtyła|Wiki Loves Peace|Uploaded via Campaign:Wiki Loves Peace

ImageDescription.value:
Tribute to the "Messenger of Peace", who dedicated his life and pontificate to tearing down walls, uniting wills, and building bridges between nations and religions. His tireless diplomatic work averted wars and reminded the world that harmony is only born from mutual respect.

His pontificate of nearly 27 years was deeply marked by international diplomacy, interreligious dialogue, and active opposition to war.


Historical Actions in Favor of Peace:

  • Mediation in the Beagle Conflict (1978): He averted an imminent war between Argentina and Chile over territorial disputes. His direct diplomatic intervention led both countries to sign the Treaty of Peace and Friendship in 1984.
  • Support for the Solidarity Movement in Poland: His defense of human rights and his historic trips to his native Poland (especially in 1979 and 1983) weakened the legitimacy of the communist regime. He peacefully backed Lech Wałęsa’s independent trade union, accelerating the democratic transition in Eastern Europe without bloodshed.
  • Forgiveness as a Tool for Peace (1983): After surviving an assassination attempt in 1981, he visited his attacker, Mehmet Ali Ağca, in prison to publicly forgive him, giving a living example of reconciliation.
  • Approaching Judaism and Islam: He was the first modern Pope to enter a synagogue (Rome, 1986), where he called Jewish people our "elder brothers." He also became the first Pontiff to visit a mosque (Damasco, 2001) and to pray at the Western Wall in Jerusalem.
  • The World Day of Prayer for Peace in Assisi (1986): For the first time in history, he brought together leaders of the world's major religions (Christians, Jews, Muslims, Buddhists, Hindus) to pray together for peace, setting a precedent for global unity.
  • Opposition to the Gulf and Iraq Wars (1991 and 2003): He firmly opposed military interventions in the Middle East. In 2003, he sent diplomatic envoys to Washington and Baghdad in an attempt to stop the invasion of Iraq.
  • Defense of Human Rights: Known as the "Pilgrim Pope," he used his more than 100 international trips to denounce human rights violations by both right-wing dictatorships in Latin America and totalitarian left-wing regimes.
  • Message Against the Arms Race: In his speeches before the United Nations (UN) and in his annual messages for the World Day of Peace, he harshly criticized excessive military spending and advocated for a social order grounded in justice, freedom, and love.


His Speeches Before the UN and His Encyclicals Left Universal Messages in Favor of Peace:

  • "War is a failure for humanity." (Spoken during the Balkans conflict in the 1990s).
  • "There is no peace without justice, there is no justice without forgiveness." (Message for the World Day of Peace, 2002).
  • "Development is the new name for peace." (Echoing that poverty and inequality are the root causes of conflict).
  • "Never again war! Never again war! Which destroys the lives of innocent people, teaches how to kill, and throws into upheaval even the lives of those who do the killing." (Urgent appeal during the Day of Prayer for Peace).
  • "Peace is not written with letters of blood, but with letters of intellect and heart." (Message addressed to youth during his international trips).
  • "Forgiveness is the key to peace in the world, because a peace that does not spring from the sincere forgiveness of hearts will always be a fragile peace."
  • "Peace is not just the absence of war; it is respect for the rights of man." (Speech underlining that true peace requires just social conditions).
  • "If you want peace, defend life." (Message directly linking respect for human dignity from its beginning with global social stability).
  • "Do not be afraid." (His most famous phrase from the beginning of his pontificate in 1978, used countless times to encourage oppressed peoples to seek freedom peacefully).


Facts About the Sculpture:

  • Location: John Paul II Square, Brisas de Jalisco neighborhood, Jalisco parish, Motatán municipality, Trujillo state (Venezuela).
  • Material and Dimensions: It is made of bronze and stands 2.20 meters tall in a pedestrian (standing) position.
  • Creators: It was sculpted by Trujillo artists Enrique “Chan” Terán and Humphrey Accary.
  • Timeline and Casting: Its creation took approximately two months, and the piece was cast in the city of Mérida.
  • Inauguration: It was inaugurated in 2009 as a tribute to the beloved Pope, who visited Venezuela twice and was a great champion of peace.
